headline: Committee reviews Vehicle Disposal Fee Fund, takes no legislative action

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The department said it wants the $25 vehicle registration fee to stay at $25 because substantial capital project costs are coming. The chair said possible uses of the fund will be explored another day.
meeting.recap: The committee reviewed the Vehicle Disposal Fee Fund and Program, item BFED 2032.[[0:16:58]] Drivers pay a $25 fee into the fund each time they register a car.[[0:17:24]] Finance reported average yearly collections of about $4.2 million for fiscal years 21 through 26.[[0:17:36]] The chair said no legislative action would be taken on this item.[[0:18:03]] A deputy director said the fund balance was $19,213,139 as of August 28th.[[0:19:13]] A testifier asked the committee to consider changing the rules to expand use of the program.[[0:30:00]] A department official said they are studying a Hawaiʻi Island program as a model.[[0:36:52]] The official said the fund already pays to remove abandoned vehicles from County property.[[0:37:06]] The official said the County could potentially amend Chapter 3.27 to expand how the money is used.[[0:46:27]] The official said electric vehicles are being stockpiled because permitting and shipping limits halted their processing.[[0:58:47]] A council member asked whether the $25 fee could be reduced to $10.[[1:10:37]] The department said it wants the fee to stay at $25 because substantial CIP (capital project) costs are coming.[[1:11:00]]
meeting.next: The chair said the committee will send a member's question about a battery processing or holding facility to the department. The chair said possible uses of the fund will be explored another day. A department official offered to provide data on how soon vehicles are towed after a police report.

moments.q: Electric vehicles "being stockpiled at the moment"
"We would like to see the $25 remain at $25."
